arXiv:2610.28095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states offer a promising alternative for capturing Landau level (LL) mixing and for understanding FQH physics, yet the incorporation of physical priors has so far been limited to the minimal exact constraints built into the ansatz. item.title: Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Phase Optimization Complexity in Variational Wave Functions for Heisenberg Antiferromagnets
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Mahmud Ashraf Shamim, Md Moshiur Rahman Raj, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Paulo T Araujo
arXiv:2602.04943v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the computational complexity of learning the ground state phase structure of Heisenberg antiferromagnets. Representing Hilbert space as a weighted graph, the variational energy defines a weighted XY model that, for Z₂ phases, reduces to a classical antiferromagnetic Ising model on that graph. For fixed amplitudes, reconstructing the signs of the ground state wavefunction thus reduces to a weighted Max-Cut instance. This links sign optimization of wavefunctions directly to combinatorial optimization.

item.title: Quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold networks are classically reproducible at their attained accuracy, and a discrete-logarithm encoding need not be: a measurement-based map of where quantum advantage can live
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hikaru Wakaura
Quantum machine-learning models are useful only if classical computers cannot cheaply imitate them. We test this directly for quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (QKANs)---neural networks whose tunable ``activation functions'' are small quantum circuits---by asking whether each model can be contracted as an efficient tensor network (TN). Our task-aware yardstick is the bond dimension a classical surrogate needs to copy the model's output at the accuracy the model itself reaches. We find a clear ladder. The amplitude-encoded Chebyshev QKAN uses only logarithmically many qubits and is exactly classical.
